governanceNotes: D1 batch 33 (2026-09-23): deferred on duplicate-scope grounds under the diabetes-mellitus (batch 22) and eczema (batch 27) precedents. The catalog alias for this identity is 'gynecologic disorders' - a class label rather than a disease entity - and the genitourinary-gynecological catalog carries the typed children endometriosis, ovarian-cysts, pelvic-inflammatory-disease, polycystic-ovary-syndrome, uterine-fibroids, and vaginismus, plus ovarian-cancer under the oncological schedule; four of the six typed children already carry published outgoing edges (endometriosis -> ovarian-cancer and -> depressive-disorder, pelvic-inflammatory-disease -> ovarian-cancer, polycystic-ovary-syndrome -> endometrial-cancer and -> depressive-disorder, uterine-fibroids -> anemia and -> endometriosis). Any edge authored under this umbrella would restate one typed child's pathway under a class identity, creating a parallel pathway that double-counts the same disease process.

Negative screen recorded 2026-09-23: a class identity has no condition-specific literature of its own - PubMed evidence for any gynecologic-outcome claim resolves to named diseases (endometriosis, PCOS, fibroids, PID, ovarian pathology) whose evidence bases are already or will be carried by their own identities - so no condition-specific source set exists for this identity. Reopening condition: a qualified-human governance decision on the umbrella's scope, or a documented pathway attributable to the class as such that no typed child carries (the class-merge or new-typed-child scenario).
